title: Security posture discovery - Verity Health
summary: Intro call to understand Verity Health security and compliance needs for adopting Redwood. Key topics: SOC 2 / ISO certification, SSO/SAML and SCIM, RBAC and least privilege, audit logs and retention, encryption and KMS integrations, data residency and retention policies. Customer leaning toward Dedicated or Private deployment; next step is sharing SOC2/ISO artifacts and scheduling technical deep dive for VPC architecture and demo of audit logs.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment
action_items: Samantha Lee - send SOC 2 Type II report and ISO summary (due 2026-06-18)
Daniel Park - prepare VPC/private deployment architecture diagram and example audit log export (due 2026-06-20)
Priya Shah - share list of mandatory compliance controls and data residency constraints (due 2026-06-22)
next_steps: Share VPC architecture diagram and sample audit log
Schedule technical deep-dive with Verity infra team (proposed: 2026-06-23)
Run a short benchmark of inference latency for a 2k token workload in Dedicated mode if Verity requests
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (CISO - Verity), Mark Lewis (Head of Eng), Emily Tran (DevOps)

00:00 Samantha Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Samantha with Redwood Inference i run the enterprise motion here. quick check — can you hear me okay?
00:05 Priya Shah: yes loud and clear, thanks Samantha.
00:08 Samantha Lee: awesome. quick agenda, we want to understand your security posture and requirements around SOC2 / ISO, sso and provisioning, audit and retention, encryption/KMS, and then talk deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Daniel will chime in for technical detail.
00:22 Mark Lewis: sounds good. for context we are Verity Health, about 2k employees, PHI in some workflows, currently evaluating LLMs for triage assistant and internal summarization. our main constraint is regulatory - HIPAA-adjacent and several enterprise contracts require SOC2 and strict auditability.
00:38 Daniel Park: understood. quick question on data flows — will inference touch raw PHI or will you always redact client identifiers before sending?
00:45 Emily Tran: the plan today is some flows will include PHI, others will be redacted. so we need options: isolation for PHI, encryption, and strong access controls.
00:55 Priya Shah: and we need to know whether Redwood Hosted keeps any persistent copies of prompts or outputs, typical data retention windows, and where logs live.
01:05 Samantha Lee: totally. high level — Redwood Hosted is our managed offering, data at rest encrypted, we retain logs for a configurable period; default shorter retention for hosted customers. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with data isolation and can be configured with longer retention or custom policies; Private (VPC or on-prem) gives the most control — data never leaves your VPC and you bring your own KMS if needed.
01:25 Priya Shah: are you SOC 2 Type II and ISO certified?
01:29 Samantha Lee: we are SOC 2 Type II compliant — we'll share the report under an NDA — and we have ISO 27001 alignment, i will attach the summary.
01:37 Priya Shah: okay please share. can you also share details on audit logs — what's captured, and can we forward logs to our SIEM?
01:44 Daniel Park: yes, good question. audit logs capture request metadata (timestamp, request id, model/version, route, token counts), auth events (api key usage, sso logins), and admin/role changes. we provide a streaming export to customer S3 or syslog endpoint for Dedicated and Private; hosted customers can request log exports or use the logging api — we'll include an example. note: we do obfuscate or redact sensitive fields in logs by default for hosted.
02:10 Mark Lewis: obfuscate fields — do you allow full text of prompts in the logs for Dedicated? we need the ability to audit full prompts for certain contracts.
02:19 Daniel Park: Dedicated can be configured to persist prompts in logs in a controlled manner and ship to your S3 with lifecycle policies. for Private, you control everything.
02:27 Priya Shah: what about SSO — SAML and SCIM? we use Okta and need provisioning and just-in-time access.
02:33 Samantha Lee: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning, roles sync, and group mapping. you can map your IdP groups to RBAC roles. we also support session length controls and automatic re-auth.
02:47 Emily Tran: for RBAC how granular are roles? can we do least-privilege so only certain teams can call models that access PHI?
02:55 Daniel Park: yes — roles are resource scoped: you can define per-route or per-model permissions plus environment-level roles. we also integrate with your IdP so role assignment is handled via SCIM group membership. there is an admin role, developer role, ops role, and you can define custom roles via the console or API.
03:14 Priya Shah: KMS — do you have native integration with customer-managed keys? we require that for on-prem or private deployments for encrypting model artifacts and logs.
03:22 Samantha Lee: we support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments. for Hosted we offer our managed KMS but can set up a customer-managed KMS through cloud key peering for some enterprise tiers. Daniel, any specifics?
03:33 Daniel Park: for AWS customers we support using your AWS KMS key with key policy to allow Redwood service role access, or in Private you can host a KMS/HSM in your network. we can document the key rotation/usage model.
03:44 Mark Lewis: data residency — we have EEA restrictions for EU patients; can we ensure data stays in eu-region?
03:50 Samantha Lee: yes, we have regionalized clusters. hosted customers can select region; Dedicated and Private give full control over placement. we can commit to region-specific processing and storage as part of contract.
04:02 Priya Shah: retention — what's default and can you set custom TTLs and deletion workflows? we need proof of deletion for certain audits.
04:10 Daniel Park: default retention in hosted is 30 days for request/response logs and 90 days for aggregated metrics; we can change that for enterprise. Dedicated/Private can implement custom TTLs and deletion hooks; we support programmatic deletion and attestations — we'll outline the process in the doc pack.
04:27 Emily Tran: regarding backups and encryption at rest for model cache and kv stores — is everything encrypted?
04:33 Daniel Park: yes, encryption at rest is standard; caches and KV store use encrypted volumes. for Dedicated we can encrypt with your KMS key. snapshots/backups are also encrypted and can be restricted to your customer account.
04:47 Priya Shah: any notable exceptions or limitations we should know about for hosted? for example, are there any staff access paths to data or keys?
04:55 Samantha Lee: we enforce least-privilege internally; staff access to customer data is controlled via break-glass with audit trails and is rare — typically for incident response. SOC 2 controls and internal RBAC govern that. we'll include our access control policy summary.
05:10 Mark Lewis: performance — we might want to run a POC and measure latency for our 2k token workloads; if we go Dedicated we need guaranteed throughput. can you do a POC on Dedicated?
05:21 Samantha Lee: yes, Dedicated reserved capacity is available and we can provision a short-term eval pool for a POC. we'll need to size based on expected qps and sequence lengths — Daniel can follow up on sizing. also we can show pricing for Dedicated vs hosted with and without caching/quantization.
05:36 Daniel Park: for benchmarks we usually run a sim load with your payload distribution; for PHI flows we'd recommend Private or Dedicated with strict logging configs.
05:45 Priya Shah: contractually we need indemnities around data handling and an audit clause. is Redwood willing to include audit rights and SOC2 attachments?
05:54 Samantha Lee: yes, we include SOC2 attachments and offer audit rights for enterprise buys; legal can provide standard language, or we can negotiate per-customer.
06:02 Emily Tran: one more technical — how do you handle long-term KV cache and potential leakage? we want to ensure PHI isn't cached where it could be served to other tenants.
06:12 Daniel Park: by default caches are tenant-isolated; persistent KV can be disabled or encrypted with your keys. we also have TTLs on cache entries and can exclude certain routes from caching. we'll provide config examples.
06:26 Priya Shah: great. any third-party penetration test reports or vuln scans?
06:30 Samantha Lee: we do regular pen tests and vuln scanning; summary reports can be shared under NDA.
06:36 Mark Lewis: ok next steps?
06:38 Samantha Lee: i'll email the SOC2 Type II report and ISO summary, daniel will attach a VPC/private deployment diagram and sample audit log export, and we'd like to set a technical deep-dive next week with your infra team.
06:48 Priya Shah: sounds good. i'll also send a list of mandatory controls we need to include.
06:53 Samantha Lee: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pack and proposed times.
06:58 Meeting end

Notes on transcript: occasional minor transcription errors (names sometimes mis-typed), natural crosstalk, and some shorthand. The team referenced shared artifacts: "SOC2 report (link)" "VPC architecture diagram (to be sent)" and "sample audit logs (S3 export)" which will be attached to the follow-up email.
